options: ServiceNow's name for the underlying application-development platform that ITSM and every other ServiceNow product is built on
Another name for the Incident Management module only
A separate product customers must buy in addition to ServiceNow
A reporting dashboard inside ITOM
questions.explain: The Now Platform is the shared engine — tables, forms, workflow, scripting — underneath every ServiceNow application, including ITSM.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the real applications built on the Now Platform mentioned in this lesson?
options: HR Service Delivery
Customer Service Management (CSM)
Security Operations (SecOps)
Microsoft Excel Online
questions.explain: Excel Online is a Microsoft product, not a ServiceNow application. ITSM, ITOM, ITBM, HR Service Delivery, CSM, SecOps, and Source-to-Pay are all real Now Platform applications.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say the incident table isn't architecturally special?
options: It's a database table built with the same tools (Form Designer, Business Rules, Client Scripts) available to any custom application on the platform
Because incidents are actually stored outside the ServiceNow database
Because Incident Management doesn't use tables at all
Because only ServiceNow employees can edit the incident table
questions.explain: Incident Management is just an application like any other — its table, form, and logic use the same underlying platform mechanisms available to any custom-built app.

questions.q: Why do job postings typically say "ServiceNow Administrator" rather than "ITSM Administrator"?
options: ITSM administrator roles don't exist
The market treats ServiceNow as a transferable platform skill, not a skill tied to one specific application suite
ServiceNow doesn't support ITSM anymore
Administrators never touch ITSM at all
questions.explain: Because the underlying platform skills (tables, forms, workflow, scripting, security) transfer across whichever applications — ITSM, HR, CSM, custom apps — an employer happens to run.

questions.q: What does "scoped application" mean in ServiceNow?
options: A self-contained application — its own tables, logic, and UI — built on the Now Platform and isolated from other apps
A limited-time trial version of ITSM
An application that can only be used by ServiceNow support staff
A synonym for the CMDB
questions.explain: Scoped applications are how custom and third-party apps are built and isolated on top of the shared Now Platform.
